newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rebel attack kills 19 in Sri Lanka's northeast.
newsitem.headline: Rebel attack kills 19 in Sri Lanka's northeast.

text.p: Separatist Tamil rebels attacked a remote police station in Sri Lanka's northeast early on Monday, killing at least 14 policemen and wounding more than 16 others, security forces officials in the area said.

Five civilians were also killed when Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels attacked the police station at Morawewa in the Trincomalee district, 240 km (150 miles) northeast of the capital Colombo, they said.
More than 200 rebels are believed to have taken part in the attack, which took place shortly after midnight (1800 GMT) on Sunday, they added.
"Many civilians were killed and wounded from the firing because they rushed out of their homes in panic and began running for cover," a police officer told Reuters.

Among the dead were 11 constables, three civilian homeguards and five civilians. Homeguards are trained and armed civilians assigned to guard remote police stations in the island's north and east where the LTTE are fighting to establish an independent homeland.

Officials said at least 13 constables, three homeguards and five more civilians were wounded in the attack, which lasted for about two hours. No details were available on the number of LTTE dead or wounded.
